name: Auxiliary session action only (sts:SetSourceIdentity) with an external-account principal - session-control, NOT cross-account assume
note: IAM-805 iteration 3 blocking-defect regression. A statement whose ONLY action is an auxiliary session action (sts:SetSourceIdentity) grants no ability to assume the role, even when it names an external account/root principal. It must be classified as an informational session-control capability, NEVER a high TRUST-CROSS-ACCOUNT 'delegates assume-role' finding (that asserts an assumption the action does not grant - threat-model T8).
rationale: sts:SetSourceIdentity only PERMITS setting a source identity on the session; it is required in the trust policy for the role to accept a source identity, but it is an accountability/traceability control, not an assume grant (trust-policy-semantics 3, source 9). AWS evaluates the assume action and this auxiliary action for the SAME caller, so an external account that cannot already assume the role via a separate sts:AssumeRole* grant never reaches sts:SetSourceIdentity - the statement is inert. Naming an external account/root principal on an aux-only statement does NOT delegate assume-role to that account; classifying it as a high cross-account trust ('any identity the trusted account authorizes can assume this role') would assert an assumption the action does not convey (threat-model T8). The correct classification is an informational session-control capability whose prose never claims assumption. Ref: AWS Monitor and control actions taken with assumed roles (sts:SetSourceIdentity); docs/trust-policy-semantics.md sec 3.
